title: Sprint-weave applied-ml quant synthesis - Jun 25 2026
content:
Meeting: Applied ML weekly research — quantization + onboarding synthesis
Date: 2026-06-25
Owner / note taker: Marisol Chen
Attendees: Marisol, Aiden, Sofia, Ellen, Ravi (brief), + async updates from Anu/Vik
Location: Zoom / #applied-ml Slack

High-level goal for week: pull together the last two microbench rounds and the eval sweep, produce a short checklist for safe model-onboarding for the compact-quant profile, and identify 2 regressions to triage before we promote compact-quant to canary on Dedicated.

---
Standup snippets (quick):
- Aiden: finished kv-cache prefetch instrumentation, saw ~8% throughput improvement for 4k context with microbatch size 16; still investigating schedule jitter at 95th p95.
- Sofia: ran full eval sweep (qa/summary/code-gen) on client-sample-17; compact-quant v1 shows +2.6% exact-match drop on short-answer QA, but no major hallucination shift.
- Ellen: profiling LLM kernels — attention matmul path introduces extra memcopy in TF32 path on our Nvidia nodes under certain sequence alignments; working on patch to avoid copy.
- Ravi: onboarding checklist draft updated; added optional per-customer eval set step.

---
Key experiment results (summary):
1) Microbench: compact-quant v1 (8-bit asymmetric + per-channel) on a-reserved-rtg cluster
   - Throughput (tokens/s): baseline fp16=5200, compact-quant=4700 (approx -9.6%)
   - Median latency per token: baseline fp16=9.2ms, compact-quant=9.9ms (+7.6%)
   - Memory usage (model+kv): baseline fp16=38GB, compact-quant=26GB (-31%)
   Notes: perf drop larger at tail when microbatch=1 and seqLen>2048; microbatching to 4 recovers ~+5% throughput.

2) Eval sweep (client-sample-17, 3k prompts across QA, summarization, code-gen)
   - QA short-answer EM: baseline fp16=72.4%, compact-quant=70.5% (delta -1.9 absolute)
   - Summarization ROUGE-L: baseline=34.8, compact-quant=34.5 (-0.3)
   - Code-gen pass@1: baseline=41.2, compact-quant=39.7 (-1.5)
   - Safety heuristics: token-level toxicity false positives unchanged; minor increase in repetition detection in very long contexts.
   Notes: regression concentrated on prompts with numeric reasoning and tight context truncation.

3) Kernel patch trial (Ellen's change)
   - Eliminates an unnecessary memcopy on attention path for TF32 on Ampere nodes.
   - Local bench: p95 latency down by 6% on 2 nodes for seqLen 4096.
   - Still needs integration test; potential ripple on CUDA memory allocator behavior.

---
Emergent issues / anomalies:
- Regression fingerprint: several failing QA items are dominated by rounding/truncation in linear layers when quantized scales are computed per-block instead of per-channel. Hypothesis: per-block scale is too coarse for narrow numeric tokens. Action: run a per-channel only pass on the failing set overnight. Owner: Sofia. Due: 2026-06-26 EOD.
- Tail-latency jitter after autoscaler events: observed 200–400ms spikes correlated with re-warming KV cache on new instances. Action: Aiden to add warm-start prefetch at instance join and flag tests in canary. Owner: Aiden. Due: 2026-07-01.
- Memory allocator edge-case with Ellen's kernel patch: sporadic OOM when running multiple models concurrently under stress. Action: Rachel (infra) to pair with Ellen to add allocator guardrails. Owner: Ellen + Rachel. Due: 2026-06-29.
---
Onboarding checklist (proposed, condensed):
1) Model artifact validation: size, sha256, architecture metadata.
2) Baseline fp16 microbench on target cluster (throughput/latency/mem).
3) Compact-quant trial microbench (microbatch sweep: 1,4,8) — report p50/p95/p99.
4) Eval sweep with customer-relevant prompt set (QA, summarization, code-gen) and default quality thresholds.
5) Regression fingerprinting: run failing-set diff, capture logits diff and token-level divergence.
6) Fallback policy: configured in route to fall back to fp16 at route-level on quality regression.
7) Rollout: internal-canary -> dedicated-canary -> gradual-split traffic -> full.
Notes: added optional step "per-customer eval" for high-risk customers (financial/legal). Reviewer: Ravi.

---
Decision log / proposals for this week:
- Promote compact-quant to internal canary only if per-channel pass resolves numeric regression and microbench shows <5% throughput regression for typical microbatch sizes. (Decision: soft, pending Sofia results)
- Keep compact-quant disabled for customers with strict numeric accuracy needs until we have per-customer eval gating.

---
Action items (owner, what, due):
- Sofia Martínez: run per-channel quant pass for failing QA subset; post results + minimal repro dataset. Due 2026-06-26 EOD.
- Aiden Park: implement warm-start prefetch heuristic for KV cache and add a microbench to simulate autoscaler churn. Due 2026-07-01.
- Ellen Brooks: land kernel memcopy patch behind feature-flag; add allocator checks with Rachel. Run integration heat test. Due 2026-06-29.
- Marisol Chen: synthesize canary checklist doc and map to rollout stages in Confluence. Due 2026-06-28.
- Ravi Kapoor: finalize onboarding checklist PR and tag security for review. Due 2026-06-27.

---
Open questions / discussion items for next meeting:
- Should we add an automated numeric-sensitivity score to model metadata (e.g., "numeric-stability: low|med|high")? If so, define evaluation metric and thresholding logic. (Tentative: discuss with SRE + product)
- How aggressively do we want microbatch defaults for compact-quant on Dedicated? Default to 4 to balance throughput/latency? Need ops input on latency SLO tradeoffs.
- Do we want a lightweight floating-point fallback for a small set of tokens (numeric tokens) instead of full per-instance fallback? Research idea: hybrid token-level dequantization.

---
Notes to self / scratch (informal):
- Quick wins: per-channel scalers seem promising and cheap to re-run. If it fixes the QA hits, we can proceed to canary.
- Keep an eye on code-gen pass@1 regression — could be brittle to small logits shifts. Might require prompting tweaks or calibration layers.
- Consider flagging customer routes that hit >2% quality delta during canary to auto-rollback.

Next meeting: 2026-07-02, 10:00 PT — quick sync + decision on canary promotion.

Appendix (links / artifacts):
- PR for microbatch instrumentation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/4213
- Confluence playbook (working draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AM/quant-onboard-playbook

End of notes.
